problem: The lead says fugacity is used 'because μ has no absolute zero'. Chemical potential does have a zero on a chosen scale; what makes it awkward is the arbitrary standard-state (reference) term. A student may take the sentence literally.
fix: Say: fugacity is used because μ_i contains an arbitrary standard-state reference μ_i°, which cancels between phases but makes absolute μ_i values meaningless.

problem: The lead states without qualification that the two phases share the same pressure. The curved-interface exception (P^α ≠ P^β) appears only later in Section 1 and in Q6, so the lead contradicts the rest for a careful reader.
fix: Add 'for a flat interface' to the lead, or note in the lead that a curved interface allows a pressure jump supported by surface tension.

problem: The first derivative ln(x₁/x₂) + A(1 − 2x₁) is only correct if x₂ is treated as dependent on x₁. The text never says x₂ = 1 − x₁ before differentiating, so a student may differentiate as if x₁ and x₂ were independent.
fix: Before differentiating, write: with x₂ = 1 − x₁, d/dx₁ of (x₁ ln x₁ + x₂ ln x₂) is ln(x₁/x₂).

problem: 'Some syllabi call the first equality the criterion of equilibrium' is ambiguous: the 'first equality' listed earlier is T^α = T^β. A student can read it as the thermal equality.
fix: Write: 'the equality of chemical potentials (or of fugacities) is called the criterion of equilibrium; this curvature test is called the criterion of stability.'

problem: The text switches from (∂²G/∂x₁²)_{T,P} to 'this expression' 1/x₁ + 1/x₂ − 2A, which is d²(g^M/RT)/dx₁². The two differ by the factor RT, so the words 'equivalently this expression > 0' mix a J/mol quantity with a dimensionless one.
fix: State (∂²G/∂x₁²)_{T,P} = RT · d²(g^M/RT)/dx₁², so the sign test is the same for both.

problem: 'The binodal is the common-tangent line' is loose: the common tangent is a construction; the binodal is the curve (locus) of the compositions of the two coexisting phases.
fix: Say: the binodal is the locus of coexisting phase compositions, obtained from the common tangent (equal chemical potentials) on the g^M curve.

problem: 'They differ by pressure and composition' does not say how. A student cannot tell that f_i = φ_i p_i = φ_i y_i P.
fix: Write: the fugacity coefficient relates the two through the partial pressure, f_i = φ_i p_i = φ_i y_i P, so φ_i is dimensionless and f_i carries Pa.
